name: Sky manta
notes: Origin at the body centre, head +Z, up +Y, 22 m wingspan, about 15 m nose to tail tip. Joints wave -1...1 (inner wing 16 deg, outer wing 10 deg more, positive lifts both tips), bank -1...1 (bank hinges at x = +-2.2 m, 15 deg each, positive drops the right wing and lifts the left), fins 0...1 (cephalic fins unroll 70 deg about X, forward and down), glow 0...1 are empty drivers; child parts mimic them. Five spot lamp parts (lampsC, lampsR1, lampsR2, lampsL1, lampsL2) follow their wing segment and switch option at glow 0.05 (emissive cyan spots, one cyan point light).
parts: flat body lofted spanwise, 64 stations by 64 radial points, swept planform, thick central disc thinning to the wing tips
dark slate dorsal skin over a white belly (separate lofts)
wings split into inner and outer segments on hinges for tip flex
two cephalic fins either side of a wide mouth, eyes on the head sides
five gill slits per side on the underside
bioluminescent spot rows along the wings and a scatter over the disc
style: Giant oceanic manta ray that flies: smooth wet dark skin with a white belly, bioluminescent cyan spot pattern on the back. Original design.
summary: 22 m sky manta ray: lofted flat body with flexing wing tips, cephalic fins, gill slits, dark top and white belly, bioluminescent cyan spots, whip tail.
